title: Load without hiding bugs
prompt: `Store` is supplied. `Store.Load(key)` returns the stored text, which may be an empty string. It throws `InvalidOperationException` when the store is offline, and `ArgumentException` when the key is empty. Write `public static string SafeLoad(string key)`. Return what `Load` returns, including an empty string. When the store is offline, return `"unavailable"`. An `ArgumentException` is a bug in the caller, so let it pass through uncaught.
hints: Which of the two exception types is an expected failure here, and which is a bug?
A catch block handles only the type it names. Name the one you can handle.
Wrap Store.Load(key) in try, and add catch (InvalidOperationException) that returns "unavailable". Do not test the returned text.
checkLabels: A stored value must be returned unchanged.
An empty stored value is a success and must be returned as empty text.
When the store is offline, the result must be "unavailable".
An empty key must still throw an ArgumentException.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Catches every exception, which hides the caller's bug.
Treats an empty result as a failed load.

feedback: Look at which exception type your catch names, and whether an empty result is passed on unchanged.
